name: Graph Convolutional Network (GCN)
analogy: Think of it as every instrument at a trading floor taking an evenly weighted poll of its neighbors before forming a view. Each desk averages its own reading with the readings of the desks next to it, and after a couple of rounds every desk has a view colored by its whole neighborhood.

steps.title: Build the network of instruments
steps.description: Each instrument is a node and a link joins two nodes when they are meaningfully related, for example when their returns have recently moved together. The pattern of links is fixed for the run.
steps.inExample: Five equity index futures are nodes; links join those whose recent 5-minute returns agreed more than 50 percent of the time.

steps.title: Give every node its own facts
steps.description: Each node carries a row of numbers describing it: recent returns, range, volume ratio and similar readings. These are what get passed around.
steps.inExample: MNQ carries a 6-bar return, average true range, relative strength index and volume ratio.

steps.title: Average over the neighborhood
steps.description: Each node replaces its description with an average of its own and its neighbors' descriptions. The average is balanced so that a node with many links is not drowned out or inflated compared with one with few.
steps.inExample: MNQ's description becomes a balanced average of its own readings and those of its four linked neighbors, ES and three other index futures.

steps.title: Apply a learned transformation
steps.description: The averaged description is passed through a learned set of weights and a bending rule, the same weights for every node. This is where the network learns which combinations of neighbor features are useful.
steps.inExample: The averaged readings are turned into 16 new numbers that emphasize shared momentum and a joint volume surge.

steps.title: Repeat to widen the view
steps.description: The averaging and transformation are done again, so each node now hears from neighbors of its neighbors. Two rounds cover things two links away; many more rounds tend to blur all nodes into the same view.
steps.inExample: After the second round, MNQ's description also carries what ES itself learned from its own neighbors in the first round, not just the raw readings.

steps.title: Read the answer for each node
steps.description: A final layer converts each node's description into an output, such as a direction probability or a regime label. Training compares these outputs with real outcomes and adjusts the shared weights.
steps.inExample: The MNQ node outputs a 56 percent probability of a higher close 6 bars later.

useFor.task: Predicting one market with help from linked markets
useFor.example: Estimating MNQ's next-30-minute direction using the returns and volume of ES and other index futures through the network.
Labeling each bar risk-on or risk-off from the joint state of equity, rate and volatility series.

useFor.task: Smoothing noisy signals across related series
useFor.example: Pulling a thin market's noisy volume reading toward the typical reading of its linked markets.

useFor.task: Finding clusters of assets that behave alike
useFor.example: Using the learned node descriptions to group instruments that move together, as an input to diversification checks.

avoidWhen: The links between instruments change quickly; the averaging weights here are fixed by the graph, so an attention-based graph model that re-weights neighbors on the fly adapts better.
Only one instrument is involved; a graph of one node adds nothing, so a feature-table or sequence model is the better fit.

example.scenario: At the 11:30 bar, a Graph Convolutional Network over five US index futures is asked for the probability that MNQ's close 6 bars (30 minutes) later is higher.

input.summary: Five nodes with features, joined by a graph of recent return agreement.

fields.name: MNQ return over the last 6 bars
fields.meaning: Recent 30-minute change of the node being predicted.

fields.name: ES return over the last 6 bars
fields.meaning: Recent 30-minute change of the most closely linked neighbor.

fields.name: MNQ volume against its 20-bar average
fields.meaning: Trading is moderately heavier than normal.

fields.name: MNQ average true range, 14 bars
fields.meaning: How much MNQ has been moving per bar.

fields.name: links to MNQ
fields.meaning: How many neighbors are averaged into the MNQ node.

fields.name: rounds of averaging
fields.meaning: How far information travels across the network.

output.summary: A direction probability for each node; MNQ's is shown.

fields.name: probability the close is higher 6 bars later
fields.meaning: The MNQ node's final answer after two rounds of neighborhood averaging.

fields.name: call
fields.meaning: The side the probability falls on when the dividing line is 50 percent.

example.reading: A 56 percent lean built largely from a close neighbor is a mild tilt. Check that it beats simply following ES's recent move, and judge it on net result after commission and slippage across walk-forward folds.
